Federal

FED-ur-uhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Federal is relating to a national government made up of united states or regions.

National parks are cared for by the federal government.

Worked Example

Mail delivery is a federal service that works the same in every state.

The mail works the same across all fifty states because the national government runs it. Things run by that government are federal.

How Federal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

national

national: for the whole country

governmental

governmental: relating to government

Antonyms

local

local: of the nearby area

state

state: run by one state, not the whole country

How Strong Is It? — Statewide → International → federal

Statewide vs. federal

Statewide vs. federal: Statewide is smaller: a statewide contest includes just one state.

International vs. federal

International vs. federal: International is bigger: international rules stretch across many countries, even bigger than one nation.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — feder

root — feder: treaty, agreement between groups (Latin (foedus, foederis))

suffix — al

suffix — al: characteristic of, relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Feder- means an agreement between groups, so federal describes a government that unites many states under one agreement.

Use the root in a new word: federation

Use the root in a new word: federation: The states joined together in a federation, agreeing to share one national government. (Federation is simply a bigger word from the same family - no everyday grade-school word shares this rare root.)
